terms.comment: The form that “shares” in noun and verb (particeps). The present participle is participium praesentis temporis, the perfect praeteritī temporis, the future futūrī (Traupman 229, 248). Quintilian calls the supine verba participiālia (1.4.29).

phrases.latin: in participiō per genus et cāsum, ut in vocābulō, per tempora, ut in verbō, per numerum, ut in utrōque, peccātur
phrases.english: in the participle one goes wrong in gender and case, as in a noun, in tense, as in a verb, and in number, as in both

phrases.latin: Dīc participium hujus verbī, praesentī tempore.
phrases.english: Give the present participle of this verb.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 229, p. 233, p. 234, p. 248.
Quintilian checked against the Perseus Latin texts, and cited by its numbering.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
